text.title: AI Pairing Decision Tree Core Rules
text.summary: 7 testable rules constraining the per-task routing record (stakes, reversibility, novelty, supervision_budget → solo | ai-pair | full-agent). Each rule is checkable against the record's fields, the repository, or the CI configuration.

rule.statement: `stakes` MUST be derived from named observables — rows or tables written, customer-facing endpoints touched, money moved, credentials or PII read, blast radius if the change is wrong — and the record names which one applies. Task size, deadline pressure and personal difficulty MUST NOT set the field.

rationale.source: Change-management risk classification (ITIL change risk / SRE production-change review)

rule.rationale: Effort and risk are uncorrelated: a one-character change to a CIDR block or a rate limit is trivial to write and takes the service down, while a 900-line vendored refactor is tedious and reversible. Scoring by effort routes exactly the wrong tasks to the least supervised mode.

rule.statement: Tasks whose revert requires a data restore or an external counterparty MUST route to `solo` or `ai-pair` with pre-merge human diff review — never `full-agent`. Enumerated: destructive migrations (`DROP COLUMN`, `DROP TABLE`, non-nullable backfill), hard deletes without a soft-delete path, payment capture or refund, outbound email/push to real users, key or secret rotation, DNS and TLS cutover, IAM policy widening, published-package release.

rationale.source: Amazon shareholder-letter type-1 / type-2 door framing; database change-management practice

rule.rationale: Reversible changes are protected by the revert, so supervision can be cheap; irreversible ones are protected only by the review that happens before they run. Automation removes precisely that review, and the failure surfaces after the only cheap remedy has expired.

rule.statement: `verdict=full-agent` is admissible only if the supervision budget covers reviewing the expected diff at a sustainable inspection rate — plan on 200–400 changed lines per review sitting and no more than ~300–500 lines per hour. A task expected to produce more MUST either be split into separately reviewable commits or routed to `ai-pair`.

rationale.source: SmartBear / Cisco peer-code-review study (~2,500 reviews): defect-discovery rate falls sharply above ~200–400 LOC per review and above ~500 LOC/hour

rule.rationale: Generation is the cheap half; review time still scales with the diff. Past the rate ceiling the reviewer stops reading and starts skimming for shape, so a large agent diff is nominally reviewed and empirically unread — the mode's speed advantage is paid for out of detection.

rule.statement: `novelty=boilerplate` or `familiar` MUST cite a concrete in-repo precedent as `path:line` found by search, not by recall. With no precedent, or when the task introduces a new external dependency or calls an internal/undocumented API, `novelty=novel-pattern` and `full-agent` is unavailable.

rationale.source: USENIX Security 2025 package-hallucination study ("We Have a Package for You!") — a large share of package names recommended by LLM-generated code do not exist

rule.rationale: Absent an in-context precedent the model falls back on the shape of its training distribution and emits plausible names — a package that was never published, a helper that exists in another framework, a config key from a different major version. These fail at import or at runtime, not at review, unless a human recognises the name as invented.

rule.statement: `verdict=full-agent` requires an automated gate that runs without the operator and blocks the merge: a named test command, a type check, and a lint, each with a non-zero exit failing the pipeline. A repository whose test command does not exist or is not wired into CI cannot yield a `full-agent` verdict for any task.

rationale.source: Continuous-delivery deployment-pipeline practice (Humble & Farley) applied to unattended generation

rule.rationale: Full-agent means the human is absent at generation time, so the gate is the only reader of the diff before it lands. Without one the verdict is not "delegated with a safety net" but "unreviewed", and the mode's whole risk model rests on a check that was never installed.

rule.statement: The record is written before the first prompt of the session; `last_touched` MUST precede the earliest timestamp in the session transcript. A mid-task mode change emits a NEW record referencing the previous `artefact_id` — the original verdict is never edited.

rationale.source: Internal — audits of retrospectively written routing records

rule.rationale: A verdict written after the work reliably matches whatever happened, so the record stops being a decision and becomes a description. Superseding rather than editing preserves the one fact the audit needs: that the operator started in agent mode and had to fall back, which is the signal that the routing questions were answered wrong.

rule.statement: Do NOT produce a record when (a) the task is a throwaway script with no commit — take whatever is fastest; (b) the change is IDE-template or codegen boilerplate with no decision to make (scaffolded migration, generated client, formatter run); (c) the repository has a standing policy that already fixes the mode for this class of change — apply the policy and cite it rather than re-deriving it per task.
rule.rationale: The record costs roughly a minute and buys an auditable choice; where the choice is forced by policy or absent by construction it buys nothing, and per-task records that all say the same thing train the operator to stop reading them.
